chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn 'Abdus ibn Ibrahim, who said:
I saw Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and he had come out from the bathhouse, and he was like the rose from his head to his feet, from the effects of the henna.

key_terms.أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ: Abu Ja'far, a title for the second Imam, Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir
key_terms.الْحَمَّامِ: the bathhouse, a place for ritual and personal cleansing
key_terms.الْحِنَّاءِ: henna, a natural dye used for beautification
key_terms.الْوَرَدَةِ: the rose, used here as a simile for redness and beauty

ai.seo_question: What did the Imam look like after applying henna?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* depicts Imam Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him) emerging from the bathhouse with his body and hair stained red by henna, likening his appearance to a rose. It underscores the Shia emphasis on *zuhrah* (beauty) and cleanliness as acts of worship, reflecting the Imam's adherence to the Sunnah of personal grooming and aesthetic refinement. The comparison to a rose symbolizes both physical purity and spiritual radiance, illustrating how the Imams embodied divine beauty in their daily lives.

en.hubeali: From him, from Ahmad Bin Ubdous Bin Ibrahim who said,

‘I saw Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> and he<sup>asws</sup> had come out from the bathhouse, and he<sup>asws</sup> was like the rose from his<sup>asws</sup> head to his<sup>asws</sup> feet, from the effects of the henna’.
en.sarwar: 4. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from Ahmad ibn ‘Ubdus ibn Ibrahim who has said the following: “
I once saw abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, coming out of the bathhouse and he looked like a flower from his top to his toes because of applying henna.’”
